choices.text: An intramolecular Claisen condensation of a diester
An intramolecular aldol reaction of a diketone
choices.why: That is the intramolecular aldol reaction of Section 23.6; the Dieckmann cyclization uses diesters.

choices.text: A mixed Claisen condensation of an ester and a ketone
choices.why: That gives a β-diketone. The Dieckmann cyclization happens within a single diester molecule.

choices.text: A conjugate addition of an enolate to an α,β-unsaturated ester
choices.why: That is a Michael reaction. The Dieckmann cyclization is a nucleophilic acyl substitution within a diester.

explanation: Intramolecular Claisen condensations of diesters, called Dieckmann cyclizations, work just as intramolecular aldol condensations of diketones do. The product is a cyclic β-keto ester.

prompt: How many atoms are in the ring of the cyclic β-keto ester formed by Dieckmann cyclization of a 1,6-diester?
explanation: Intramolecular Claisen cyclization of a 1,6-diester gives a five-membered cyclic β-keto ester; diethyl hexanedioate, for example, gives ethyl 2-oxocyclopentanecarboxylate.

prompt: How many atoms are in the ring of the product when diethyl heptanedioate, a 1,7-diester, undergoes Dieckmann cyclization?
explanation: Cyclization of a 1,7-diester gives a six-membered cyclic β-keto ester. Diethyl heptanedioate gives ethyl 2-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate.

prompt: What product forms when diethyl hexanedioate is treated with base, then H3O+?

choices.why: That six-membered ring comes from a 1,7-diester, diethyl heptanedioate.
Removing the ester group needs further steps; the Dieckmann product keeps it as a β-keto ester.
The Dieckmann product is a β-keto ester, so the ketone is on carbon 2, next to the carbon bearing the ester group.

explanation: Diethyl hexanedioate is a 1,6-diester, so it cyclizes to a five-membered cyclic β-keto ester, ethyl 2-oxocyclopentanecarboxylate (82%), with loss of ethanol.

prompt: What product would you expect from Dieckmann cyclization of diethyl 4-methylheptanedioate (sodium ethoxide, then H3O+) (Exercise 23.9.1)?

choices.why: That product comes from a 3-methyl diester. With the methyl on carbon 4, it ends up on ring carbon 5.
A heptanedioate is a 1,7-diester, which gives a six-membered ring, not five.

choices.text: A mixture of two different β-keto esters
choices.why: Carbon 4 is the middle of the chain, so the two ends of the diester are equivalent and only one product forms.

explanation: Diethyl 4-methylheptanedioate is a 1,7-diester, so it gives a six-membered cyclic β-keto ester. The ring has the –CO2Et on carbon 1, the ketone on carbon 2 and the methyl group on carbon 5: ethyl 5-methyl-2-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate.

prompt: How many different β-keto ester products does the Dieckmann cyclization of diethyl 3-methylheptanedioate give (Exercise 23.9.2)?
explanation: The diester is unsymmetrical, and each ester group can act as either the Claisen donor or the acceptor. The result is a roughly 50/50 mixture of ethyl 4-methyl-2-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate and ethyl 2-methyl-6-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate.

prompt: Why does Dieckmann cyclization of diethyl 3-methylheptanedioate give a mixture of products?

choices.text: Its two different ester groups can each act as donor and acceptor
One product has a five-membered ring and the other a six-membered ring
choices.why: Both products are six-membered cyclic β-keto esters, because the starting diester is a 1,7-diester.

choices.text: The methyl group moves to a new position during the reaction
choices.why: The methyl group stays where it is; the two products differ in which ester group became the enolate.

choices.text: The two products are double-bond isomers of one enone
choices.why: The products are β-keto esters, with no C=C; they differ in where the methyl group sits relative to the ketone and ester.

explanation: In diethyl 3-methylheptanedioate the methyl group makes the two ends different. Each ester can act as a Claisen donor and a Claisen acceptor, so the reaction gives a roughly 50/50 mixture of two β-keto esters.

prompt: The sequence (1) Dieckmann cyclization, (2) β-keto ester alkylation and (3) decarboxylation is a powerful method for preparing what?

choices.text: Open-chain β-keto esters with two alkyl groups
choices.why: The Dieckmann step makes a ring, and decarboxylation then removes the ester group.
1,5-Diketones come from Michael reactions; this sequence gives cyclic ketones.

choices.text: β-Hydroxy ketones with a new alkyl group
choices.why: Those are aldol products. This sequence gives a cyclic ketone with an alkyl group next to the carbonyl.

explanation: The cyclic β-keto ester from a Dieckmann cyclization can be alkylated and decarboxylated as in the acetoacetic ester synthesis (Section 22.7). Overall, this makes 2-substituted cyclopentanones and cyclohexanones.

prompt: Ethyl 2-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate is alkylated with sodium ethoxide and methyl iodide, CH3I, and the product is then decarboxylated. What is the final product?

choices.why: The methyl group added in the alkylation step stays on the ring; only the ester group is removed.
Alkylation occurs on the carbon between the ketone and ester groups, which becomes carbon 2 of the ketone.
The six-membered ring is unchanged by alkylation and decarboxylation.

explanation: Alkylation and subsequent decarboxylation of ethyl 2-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate yields a 2-alkylcyclohexanone. With CH3I as the alkylating agent, the product is 2-methylcyclohexanone.

prompt: Diethyl hexanedioate has ten carbon atoms. How many carbon atoms does its Dieckmann product, ethyl 2-oxocyclopentanecarboxylate, contain?
explanation: The cyclization expels ethoxide, lost as ethanol (2 carbons): 10 − 2 = 8. Ethyl 2-oxocyclopentanecarboxylate has five ring carbons plus the three carbons of –CO2Et.
